notes.title: Jumping Jazz Cats - Experimental Beta Branch - Out Now 🎮😻
notes.content:
Hello feline friends! 👋

Today, we're happy to announce that [b]we've released a Experimental Beta Branch for Jumping Jazz Cats on Steam! [/b]

This Steam Beta Branch is accessible to all, allowing you to playtest on a branch with Steam Deck Additions and Bug Fixes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/29f9a98677b0f7226779fa0002d0da39023c0e7f.png[/img]
[h3]❓ How do I access the Experimental Beta Branch?[/h3]
You can play the Beta Branch in a few simple steps, which are listed below:
[olist][*] Head to your Steam Library and find Jumping Jazz Cats.
[*] On the Jumping Jazz Cats page in Steam Library, select the Manage menu (Settings like toggle icon ⚙️).
[*] Select Properties.
[*] Select Betas.
[*] On the Beta page, click the dropdown under Beta Participation.
[*] Select the 'experimental - PUBLIC - Experimental Branch' to opt into the Beta Build.
[*] Your download of the new branch should start to download automatically. If not, close and reopen the Steam client application.[/olist]On this branch, you may experience some bugs. We have a dedicated Steam Discussions forum post, which is pinned to the Discussions page. Please use this to provide your Beta Branch feedback and to report any issues with the Experimental Beta Branch with us.

[h2]Patch Notes - Experimental Beta Build:[/h2]
[h3]Steam Deck Specific:[/h3]
[list][*] Addition of Local multiplayer (split-screen), which has been activated for Steam Deck![/list][h3]Bug Fixes:[/h3][list][*] Fixes to the UI, altering location of the golden bug score when playing in split-screen.
[*] Fixes to Ring Rally, with players now able to collect items whilst riding the Robo-vac or Dog with the special item ring.
[*] Fixes to the laser so it no longer triggers items or booster rings found in Ring Rally.
[*] Various optimizations across the game.
[*] Fixed various bugs where players could fly through the ceiling.
[*] Fixes to various effectiveness and balancing of collar tags.[/list]
[h2]Provide Feedback in our Discord Server ✅[/h2]
We also have a dedicated channel for the Experimental Beta Branch in our Discord server, so you can playtest the branch, provide feedback or find players to play with on this Beta Branch! [url=https://discord.gg/fsFxPP5B7x]Join the Le Catnip Collective server today 😸[/url]

[url=https://discord.gg/fsFxPP5B7x][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/371f46c3f8f00904121186d450a220394547106b.jpg[/img][/url]

We hope you enjoy this Beta Branch and we're looking forward to seeing your feedback on this for Steam!
[h3]Play Now! 👇😼[/h3]

notes.title: Jumping Jazz Cats Dev Blog Q&A with Dan from Le Catnip Collective
notes.content:
[h3]Hey there Feline Friends! 👋[/h3]

In today's Steam post, [b]Team17 sat down with Jumping Jazz Cat's development team at Le Catnip Collective to bring you a two-part Dev Blog![/b] 🥳

Before jumping in with the Dev Blog, earlier in the week [b]we announced our new Steam launch date for Jumping Jazz Cats - 20th May 2025![/b] We're super excited for you all to experience our kittycat party game on May 20th 😺

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/9bbca15066290c4fdd7a87d2f581000b6cfb70e5.png[/img]

In part two of our Dev Blog series, we'll be chatting with [b]Dan, Le Catnip Collective's Director & Co-Founder,[/b] to discuss Jumping Jazz Cats' origins, gaming inspirations, the party game's cat animations, and the upcoming launch on Steam! 💜

[h2]Dev Log Q&A with Daniel Harris[/h2]
[h3]How did the concept of Jumping Jazz Cats come about?[/h3]

"The concept was inspired by my love for cats and their fascinating movement. As a veteran animator, I’m constantly captivated by the way cats move—there’s such an elegant yet quirky flow to their motions. Their natural parkour-like dexterity felt like the perfect foundation for an engaging gameplay experience. I wanted to capture that unique grace and fluidity, making it both fun and challenging for players to control these jazzy, acrobatic cats in action."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/b26b314814bc66c454e9508c894335be3dc7a6a8.png[/img]
[h3]What inspired you and your team to create Jumping Jazz Cats?[/h3]

"As big fans of couch play and party games, we saw an opportunity to bring something fresh and unique to the genre by combining the fun of cat GIF antics with engaging party game mechanics. It’s not often that you see sophisticated 3D platforming integrated into a party game, and that’s something we were really excited to explore. Our goal was to create a game that’s accessible and easy for casual players to jump into, while also offering enough depth and complexity in the mechanics to keep more advanced players coming back for more. We wanted to strike that perfect balance between fun and mastery.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/02c710cdb78c5115f5da345bee539ae24d09e404.png[/img]
Also, creating a unique environment and world was a top priority for us. Drawing inspiration from nostalgic jazz, architectural themes, and the stylized art of Disney and Saturday morning cartoons, we aimed to build a beautiful, wild, and occasionally odd fantasy world for players to escape into. We wanted the environment itself to be just as engaging and immersive as the gameplay."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/cc157e3142c48cfcaa8586951a4a001a261f3992.png[/img]
[h3]How did you go about capturing the essence of cats in the game’s animations and in Jumping Jazz Cats’ gameplay?[/h3]

"A big part of capturing the essence of cats started with extensive reference study. I spent a lot of time observing frame-by-frame videos of cats in action—whether they were jumping, prowling, crawling, or pouncing. Sometimes it was about faithfully understanding the physical movements of cats and quadrupeds, while other times, it was more about emphasizing dynamic character control. To keep the gameplay engaging, I used cartoony motion to "cheat" the timing and make movement feel quicker and more fluid. I also added special effects to highlight certain actions, creating an exciting feel during key moments."

[h3]Is there one feature of the game that you are most proud of?[/h3]

"While it’s hard to pinpoint a single feature, I’m incredibly proud of how fun the game has become overall. After hundreds of hours of playtesting, our team still genuinely enjoys playing it every time. It’s amazing how often the mechanics surprise us, and that sense of discovery is something we’re truly proud of. It shows that we’ve created something that not only works, but continues to be enjoyable and exciting even after so much time."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/156a48835ac463927bbc3b955b67f8c6377b15ab.jpg[/img]
[h3]Cat games have become their own genre recently with games like [i]Stray[/i], [i]Little Kitty Big City[/i], and more! How does it feel to add another twist to the kitty game formula?[/h3]

"It’s true—there are so many new and exciting ways to experience playing as a cat now! It’s been really fun to be part of this growing trend. Being compared to such fantastic titles as [i]Stray[/i] and [i]Little Kitty Big City[/i] is an honor, as they each bring their own unique take on the cat genre. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/2c9e21ef0d898be85cd1371613e370af3944cebb.png[/img]
Our goal is to offer something different with a more quirky, cartoony vibe, and the chance to play as a wild party of cats with friends. We’re excited to offer a unique, multiplayer experience that we hope cat-game fans will really enjoy!"

[h3]Describe your emotions and how you are feeling in the lead-up to the launch![/h3]

"There are definitely a lot of emotions at this stage! I’m excited to see players around the world come together to prove their cat parkour skills. At the same time, I’m feeling a sense of relief knowing we’re about to launch our very first game. It’s such an incredible achievement for our small studio to get this project over the finish line and out into the world. We can’t wait for everyone to experience what we’ve worked so hard to create!"

[h2]Just days away from our launch...😻🗓️[/h2]
[b]Jumping Jazz Cats launches on Steam on 20th May! [/b]We're so close to our launch date and cannot wait to see you all jumping around Ellington Estate and playing our cat parkour mini-games soon! 🥳

We hope you enjoyed this Dev Blog Q&A with Dan around the development of Jumping Jazz Cats! 💜 If you missed part one of our Dev Blog with [b]Arun, Le Catnip Collective's Co-Founder, Music Composer & Sound Designer,[/b] you can read this in the post below! ⬇️

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/9bbca15066290c4fdd7a87d2f581000b6cfb70e5.png[/img]

[h3]Jumping Jazz Cats - Key Features:[/h3]
🏠 [b]Explore six varied levels:[/b] Jumping Jazz Cats blends co-operative and competitive strategies together, to create a cat party game like no-other! Each level has different objectives, some requiring you to work together with your team mates and others to get the highest score possible to claim a victory over the other team.

notes.title: Jumping Jazz Cats Dev Blog Q&A with Arun from Le Catnip Collective
notes.content:
[h3]Hey there Feline Friends! 👋[/h3]

In today's Steam post, [b]Team17 sat down with Jumping Jazz Cat's development team at Le Catnip Collective to bring you a two-part Dev Blog Q&A![/b] 🥳

In part one, we chatted with [b]Arun, Le Catnip Collective's Co-Founder, Music Composer & Sound Designer,[/b] to speak about the game's Jazz references, music inspirations, sound effects, and how Arun's feeling in the build up to Jumping Jazz Cat's Steam launch!

[h2]Dev Log Q&A with Arun Sol[/h2]
[h3]Do you have a favourite piece of music you’ve created for Jumping Jazz Cats?[/h3]

"[i]Lights Out[/i] was my favourite piece of music to create for Jumping Jazz Cats! It’s one of the ten fast-paced, jazz-inspired songs I wrote for the game.

Across the 10 songs, I took a fairly loose interpretation of the genre ‘jazz’. With [i]Lights Out[/i], for example, it’s a kind of acid jazz with a Mission Impossible-style melody. Beneath that melody, there is a thumping bass line repeating the root note of one chord. With so little variation in the chord structure, it was therefore important to add a lot of dynamics with the other instruments. To do this, I built up layers as if a DJ had sampled horn lines, a piano hook, a crazy clarinet riff, flutes, guitar, organ, and a crisp drum beat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/7ac8ce8880833a4b22e39f7310822ece05075a31.jpg[/img]
Although all of the music in Jumping Jazz Cats was composed note-by-note using MIDI, I wanted this song to actually sound like it was made up of a bunch of samples. To enhance that ‘sampled’ feel, you’ll hear throughout the song the crackle of an old record player (it’s also one of the coolest vintage sounds that exists, in my opinion!)

But what really makes the music special in Jumping Jazz Cats is that, during the chorus, something exciting changes in the game. It was therefore important to have a distinct pre-chorus to indicate that ‘something is coming’. Signalling this in [i]Lights Out[/i] is a horn-filled breakdown, with the rhythm dropping back to some swinging hi-hats.

The all-important chorus event then kicks in at the sound of a finger click, which sounds really similar to a light being turned off. After all, the song is called [i]Lights Out[/i]! The screen goes dark, and the players can only see a small area around themselves unless they eat the carrots that appear. To match the ‘dark’ vibe, the instrumentation drops back to a muffled drum and bass, and the record crackle really stands out. Then, at the end of the chorus, you hear that finger click again, and the game returns to normal. The final chorus is extra long and crescendos to one last finger click to cue the lights, and the round is over.

As you can tell, I had a lot of fun with this one!"

[h3]What games or other media forms inspired the music of Jumping Jazz Cats?[/h3]

"In the 2000s, I did a lot of Swing dance, and the music I danced to has stuck with me ever since. In fact, Dan (Le Catnip Collective's Director & Co-Founder) still does a lot of Swing dance here in Montreal where there’s a really happening scene!

But ‘Swing’ is like an umbrella term: there are all these other amazing styles pioneered by the Black jazz musicians and dancers of the first half of the 20th century. For example, there’s Balboa (a gorgeously cute style with small but blurrily fast foot movements), Lindy Hop (often danced to the big band classics, characterised by acrobatics, flashy swing-outs and incredibly cool breaks), Charleston (furious speed and fun flashiness), and Blues (very cool, very sexy, very slow).

The music of Jumping Jazz Cats is, at its heart, a tribute to Swing. I’m not actually a jazz musician, but in the 10 Song Events/gameplay songs (as well as a dozen more that play in the lobbies and menus), you’ll hear a lot of what inspires me about jazz: the organised chaos, the complexity and the catchiness, and the sheer joy of musical release."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/a713916c71107b87294931bfaf77b7c5226f0251.png[/img]
[h3]Alongside the music, you also worked on the sound effects for Jumping Jazz Cats. Could you talk us through your process for creating the sound effects for the party game?[/h3]

"At first, I tried using sounds from a soundbank: these were useful as placeholders, but they usually lacked the stylised, handmade feel we wanted to achieve. So, I then settled on an approach where most of the sounds were either A) somehow made with a jazz instrument, B) done with a voice, or C) improvised with some random object in my apartment. 

Jazz instruments are great because they have the ability to capture the cartoony silliness we were looking for. For example, with the air-dive, I used a slide whistle. To give bouncy surfaces their ‘bounce’, I used a very high note plucked on a double-bass. For the tornado boosters, I used a bass trombone slide. For the cat loaf power-up (where you get to fly) a fluttering bass trombone sounds surprisingly like a prop plane! And for the footsteps on wooden surfaces, you can tell it’s just me tapping the body of an acoustic guitar with my finger tips!

Sometimes, an effective approach was to make up sounds with my voice and then play around with effects like pitch and equalizer. For example, listen to the sound of going into and out of a nap, and you’ll realise it’s just my voice modified a bit. The catnip power-up is mostly just me doing a tongue-rolling purr. Nap in the sun and you’ll hear me doing a 3-part harmony in meows (much harder than you might think - I had to sing it extra slow so that, when I pitched it up a lot, it played at the right speed). And the hound dogs? You guessed it: it’s me barking into my microphone!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/768da4f06895b9235ed9455e7101a9769d783266.png[/img]
But my favourite use of voice is that of my daughter’s. She was 5 years old when I started working on Jumping Jazz Cats - and you can hear her cute meows by using the emote buttons (you’ll also hear her meow in our studio Le Catnip Collective’s animated logo!). Listen closely to the Lion’s Roar and you’ll hear it’s a mix of her roaring and a sample of a real lion with me growling underneath. The bee in the mini-game [i]Cat Tree Capture[/i] is another sound featuring her voice. But, at the time, she was missing all of her front teeth, so it didn’t sound bee-ish enough. I added in a real bee sound, and I wrote a flute part playing something like Flight of the Bumblebee, et voilà!

Finally, as all sound designers know, sometimes you just end up raiding the kitchen or other rooms in your home to find things to make sounds with. For example, with the scratching posts (you scratch them to change teams), I originally tried recording the sound of Velcro being ripped apart. Eventually, I settled on the sound of poppers on one of my daughter’s old onesies being unbuttoned (credit to my wife for this one!)"

[h3]Describe your emotions and how you are feeling in the lead-up to the launch![/h3]

"It’s a strange feeling!
As the co-founder of a tiny studio - we have 2 artists, 2 programmers, Dan as the director, and me doing sound design and admin - we each end up wearing many hats, and a lot weighs on our shoulders. I won’t lie: it has been stressful at times. To launch a game after almost 3 years of working on it, to have all of those hours and weeks and months and years… all leading to one single day… it’s nerve-wracking, to say the least!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/135ca066ba2a5ff338144869b4126f675f3a48d3.jpg[/img]
But for all the hard work and stress, making this game has been the most rewarding musical experience of my life.

Music is important to any game. But I am particularly proud that the music gets to be a gameplay feature in Jumping Jazz Cats. I am privileged to have worked on it with Dan, a friend of some 25 years. And I’m super proud of the wonderful and brilliant up-and-coming devs we have found in our local Quebec community. It’s a real thrill to be shipping our first game!

We also have the great fortune of being backed by Team17. They have so much publishing experience and expertise in the party-game genre (anyone heard of Overcooked?!) In the lead up to release, it’s a huge relief to have their support with the business end of things like QA, localisation, marketing etc.

Lastly, I will say that having thousands and thousands of people around the world playing our demo during Steam Next Fest was incredibly exciting! The feedback on the demo was really positive, and it felt validating of our crazy decision to make a jazzy game about jumping cats. We just hope that players will love the full game even more when it comes out on 10 April 2025!"

[h2]Jumping Jazz Cats launches on April 10th! 😻[/h2]
We'd like to say a huge thank you to you for supporting Jumping Jazz Cats! We've loved seeing your feedback, suggestions and excitement during Steam Next Fest and in the build up to launch- not far off now 👀😺

We hope you enjoyed this Dev Blog Q&A with Arun around the music and sound of Jumping Jazz Cats! Next up, we'll be chatting with Dan, Le Catnip Collective's Director & Co-Founder to discuss Jumping Jazz Cats' origins, gaming inspirations, the party game's cat animations, and the upcoming launch on Steam! 💜

notes.title: Mini-Game Deep Dive | Fat Cat & Gimme Yarn | Jumping Jazz Cats 🐈
notes.content:
[b]Hey there Feline Friends! 👋😸[/b]

We're back again this week, this time with our third Jumping Jazz Cats Deep Dive! 😼

In our previous deep-dive videos, we've covered some of Jumping Jazz Cats' mini-games, alongside our cat parkour party game's kitty customisation options! Today, we'll be covering two more of our mini-games which you can play now in our Steam Next Fest demo!

[b]Watch the full Mini-Game Deep Dive video here: ⬇️[/b]

[previewyoutube=lJrdRCWHcbc;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]🐟😻 Fat Cat [/h2]
In our minigame Fat Cat, your objective is to collect as many fish as possible to earn points! But beware, the more fish you collect, the more your stamina bar will fill up with fish, causing you to tire easily and stop you from sprinting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/2accc9d5405454140a8866635561947d304e9c33.gif[/img]

The fish will continue spawning in all sorts of quirky areas across the map, and you can get lucky
and have one appear right in front of you! This helps you when your stamina bar is jam
packed full of fish.

If you are lucky enough to have collected enough fish to fill your stamina bar, you will turn into a beach ball cat, allowing you to bounce quicker around Ellington Estate and reach higher places. The longer you can go without collecting the fish in this form though, will mean you lose your beach ball
and revert to your not so fat cat self.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/1cd9c747321b4e1225bbb70265da35d0efc2d16e.gif[/img]

[h2]🧶🐾 Gimme Yarn[/h2]
In Gimme Yarn, you and your team are tasked with collecting balls of yarn and bringing them back to your basket to earn points for your team, but watch out as other teams will be hoping to snatch your balls of yarn from right under your noses!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/83f897e88d9afa77745ca2c4c9e463c25501434b.gif[/img]

If you noticed a sneaky cat from another team trying to steal from your basket, you can equip yourself with the butterfly net and trap your opponent's. Of course, if you want to go on the offensive and kindly 😼 free up some basket space for your opponents, watch out for their nets, as they can easily send you back to your basket with your tail between your legs!

Have some of you play defence, stick around the basket and make sure your butterfly net is primed
and ready to capture all the cats! The rest of your players should go on the offensive and search the map for balls of yarn to steal and add into your teams basket! All's fair in kitty love and war! 🙀

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/1cd9c747321b4e1225bbb70265da35d0efc2d16e.gif[/img]

notes.title: Mini-Game Deep Dive | Ring Rally & Cat Tree Capture | Jumping Jazz Cats
notes.content:
[b]Hey there Feline Friends! 👋😸[/b]

We're back again this week, this time with our second Jumping Jazz Cats Deep Dive! 😼

Last time out we covered customisation in our party platformer, but this time we're going to be discussing the game mechanics of two of our six mini-games.

[b]Watch the full Mini-Game Deep Dive video here: ⬇️[/b]

[previewyoutube=tZIIyJ6HSNs;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]⭕🏁 Ring Rally[/h2]
In our minigame Ring Rally, your objective is to jump through as many hoops as possible to earn top points for you and your team. 

Wow, look at all these rings! 😻

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/c5f37dae87282e1ddd9af40557143d6dec7dddf1.gif[/img]

Don't worry if you miss one, as it will disappear behind you- just focus up on the next one and keep running through the jazzy cartoon mansion of Ellington Estate!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/0ac36c67db0c137b48b7a1cc82ffa88eae3e150c.gif[/img]

Speed is key in Ring Rally. Due to this being a race, you can utilise your Sprint to get ahead of the other kittycat players. You'll need to be careful how much you use that speed boost, as your little kitty can get tired out quickly and lose stamina.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/6aa17111fe5fe0dfa0dde1b327a157c55024cdf3.gif[/img]

Some rings are special rings, like this tambourine booster that gives you and your teammate a speed boost! Jump on through and you will get a thank you from your teammate, who enters right behind you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/77ccc5f4aff41d4558199715a5c85a396b2bd997.gif[/img]

You may have noticed another small ring amongst the others! Now that one is a good one to get,
as it will allow your kitty to gain power-ups. Each power-up is different and you never know which one you're going to get!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/9e43ccd42ab4e0bf70309dbbd76f1c1ea6a2c392.gif[/img]

[h2]🐈🌲 Cat Tree Capture[/h2]
The next mini-game we'd like to introduce you to is Cat Tree Capture! 🙀

The aim of this chaotic game is to collect as many pollen spores as possible. You may notice that the cat trees are shaped like flowers!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/6ab7c1d66d6e652c68545e9d3859679a9f2ca03a.gif[/img]

The aim of the game is to jump on the cat tree perch, causing the flower patches to fall and turn into pollen. But be careful, as other players can swoop in quick and collect that pollen from right under your nose.

Once the flower has no more petals, it will turn the colour of the player's team. This means there are no more petals to collect on this one and you must find others around the level to bounce on!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/dc141ffe9e479e1ef1323b3dd41be29de856457a.gif[/img]

Have you noticed the powerup has an image of a bee? The bee is awarded to you once you and your team take over your cat tree perches. 

It turns you into a cute busy bee that flies, allowing you to reach other flower cat trees much quicker! 🐝

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/47e51b580cd202d9dd184de84b56d72e2afc869e.gif[/img]

[h2]🎵🔨 Chorus Game - Smashing Pots[/h2]

Each Mini-Game has a Chorus Game within! This time, Smashing Pots is our Chorus Game. 

For this one, you are tasked with smashing as many pots that appear as you can, allowing you or your team to gain some extra points!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/72e5c5828027d0a67dbc5384368fb4095e862785.gif[/img]

Once you have smashed the most pots, you will automatically send a distraction on screen to your rivals... 🦇

In this case, it is a bunch of squeaky bots which are annoying but also very cute! 🥺

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/f8032de90b826f91ec9658dc29af7ce92c1d845c.gif[/img]

notes.title: Moving & Zooming! | Feline Features 1 | Jumping Jazz Cats
notes.content:
[b]Hey there Feline Friends! 👋😸[/b]

Today we're thrilled to begin [b]a new series of Steam posts titled 'Feline Features', where we look into a specific aspect of our kitty online party-game's game mechanics![/b] To kickstart this series in today's steam post, we'll be covering the movement mechanics of Jumping Jazz Cats!

To have a purr-fect party experience with our game, [b]we recommend playing Jumping Jazz Cats with a controller![/b] However, Jumping Jazz Cats can be experienced on controller and mouse and keyboard. In the post below, we've added Keyboard & Mouse but our game can also be experienced with the gamepad of your choice.

[h2]Feline Features 1 | Moving & Zooming[/h2]
We'll be starting with the very basic movements like Moving, Sprinting, and Jumping before venturing to the more exciting in-game actions like Charge Jumps, Nuzzles, and Pouncing! 

So let's begin with how to move your character:
[h3]Move[/h3]
To move your kitty character, use WASD.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/c36468c3ad6e78b9a89325b5020a4d6234eeb15a.gif[/img][h3]Sprint[/h3]
Press and hold Left Shift whilst moving to sprint. Sprinting depletes your stamina.

Your stamina is represented by the musical note on the lower part of the screen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/121de9e7935648173dc4a0328c9e906c26a484d9.gif[/img][h3]Jump[/h3]
Press Space to jump.

You can also perform a wall jump by jumping towards a wall, then as you land on it, jump off in a different direction!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/fc6e5b38b54c983eabc8234a3507e05c9e7d629b.gif[/img][h3]Catnap[/h3]
Hold Q to catnap. This will recharge your stamina bar.

Catnap until your treble clef to the left of your stamina bar is full to gain an item to use.

Recharge you stamina even faster by catnapping in warm or brightly-lit spots!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/c61a5a26eed71a6aa9d1f2b5e00d58aaaa02dc16.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/891f06849bb8790df976b6e2260afcb395692cdb.gif[/img][h3]Air Dive[/h3]
Jump then press Left Mouse Button in midair to perform a air dive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/a466d09c5501a2bdee00138b572e86795781372f.gif[/img][h3]Grab & Throw[/h3]
Press Middle Mouse Button to grab an object. Press Middle Mouse Button again to throw it.

Hold Middle Mouse Button while carrying an item to aim before throwing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/c25cec07f16f1822c3415a3774ad07236a7f55ef.gif[/img][h3]Climb[/h3]
Move towards a climable surface, then use WASD Keys to climb.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/68f81f5a09bfd20a38cd80ae8eb2ba8f424e8752.gif[/img][h3]Charge Jump[/h3]
Hold Space while standing still to charge your jump. Then release Space to perform the charge jump.

Time your charge jump perfectly to create a spring. This item will give your team a vertical boost!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/a9cac8f15867af1ef4608b66a757732ce929397d.gif[/img][h3]Nuzzle[/h3]
Press Middle Mouse Button to show you're ready to nuzzle.

If another cat does the same nearby, your nuzzling will create an item for you both!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/bbb7c69ddb17fb444e333f197e31606e0e358b16.gif[/img][h3]Pounce[/h3]
Press Left Mouse Button to pounce.

Use pouncing during the pots Chorus Minigame to break them!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/6700a6b57f58d1d2523ec729dc4acd1e30d9203d.gif[/img]
[b]We hope today has given you an insight into Jumping Jazz Cats, ready for when our demo launches (coming soon 👀) on Steam. [/b]

Get ready to to jump, bounce, and sprint around the jazzy cartoon mansion of Ellington Estate and lead your cat team to victory!

Hey all,

Firstly, we want to apologise to our community— we understand this is not the news you want to hear.
 
Releasing later in 2025 provides us with the time to polish Jumping Jazz Cats and create the best possible launch for the game we’ve been developing for the past three years. This was a tough decision, but one made to ensure we provide you with the best online party game experience.

notes.title: Jumping Jazz Cats - Cat Customisation - Deep Dive 1
notes.content:
[b]Hello feline friends! 😺👋[/b] We've just[b] posted out our first Deep Dive video, detailing our customisation menu in Jumping Jazz Cats! [/b]

Watch the full Deep Dive video to learn more about creating your dream kitty below:📺

[previewyoutube=meHpkc9FcBE;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]😼 40+ Kitty Presets[/h2]
In our customisation menu, you’ll find Pussycat Presets to select from and play as! The more games of Jumping Jazz Cats that you play, the more golden bugs you’ll earn. Spend your bugs to unlock different cat customisation cosmetics or spend them to unlock a new cat preset!

There’s 40+ cat breeds/designs to play as, so many purr-fect cats! Once you’ve selected a preset, you can customise your cat in our three tabs, body, fur and face.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/b9f9e8fea0e424b5d82230a9fb1c782818cfd6a0.gif[/img]
[h2]Customisation Menu - Body[/h2]
In the Body section, you can adjust your cats overall size, along with tail width and length. Use this menu to create the cutest and fluffiest cat possible!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/4c331695614a26f9b2cd24feadd9a0f579d26b45.gif[/img]
[h2]Customisation Menu - Fur[/h2]
The Fur menu contains multiple colour options to select from! From fur base colour, to eye colour adjustments, to changing belly fluff colour. The colour options allow for you to create a unique furball to play as!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/8406cba85af7a938647dba14990527e70571dbca.gif[/img]
[h2]Customisation Menu - Face[/h2]
The Face menu contains adjustments to the sizing of your kittycats head, ears and eyes. This tab also features options to alter your cats eye positioning, head height and the colour of your kitties eyes!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/7200d12b364ec5e23433b44fb0ff43f975b8001b.gif[/img]
[h2]💾 Save Customised Presets[/h2]
Once you’ve perfected your kitty’s design, you can save it as a customised preset! There are nine presets spaces in Jumping Jazz Cats. We've added nine presets to allow you to save multiple kitty creations at once, whilst still having the option to create more kittycats.

We hope you’re excited to create your dream feline friend or even customise your in-game kitty to look like own pet cat in Jumping Jazz Cats. We cannot wait to see your kitty creations in our cat customisation menu and hope your excited to jump in and customise your own cats when Jumping Jazz Cats launches on Steam!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42565692/0bd1c49b7aab22c817fe962725648bfe6f4fc2d4.gif[/img]
[h3]🐈 About Jumping Jazz Cats[/h3]
Two weeks ago, we announced Jumping Jazz Cats, an upcoming paw-some online party game to play with your friends! ICYMI, Jumping Jazz Cats is coming soon to Steam and can be played online for 2-9 players, offline in singleplayer trials or played locally via 4 player split screen.

You’ll play as a cat, diving, bouncing and grinding around the jazzy cartoon mansion of Ellington Estate! 

Jumping Jazz Cats features 6 chaotic online play levels, all with varied objectives including Gimme Yarn, Cat Tree Capture, Fat Cat and more. We’ll be talking mini-games more in future posts, so stay make sure to wishlist Jumping Jazz Cats to stay updated with our game! 💜

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1951780/Jumping_Jazz_Cats/

[h3]Jumping Jazz Cats - Key Features:[/h3]
😻 2-9 players online  
4️⃣ 4 local players can join via split-screen  
🏠 6 levels across the mansion to discover  
😹6 cat-GIF inspired mini-games  
🎷 10 original jazz tracks that influence gameplay during the choruses  
🕹️ Mix and match levels, mini-games and songs for immense variety  
🤝 Blend of co-operative and competitive strategies

That's all for today feline friends, see you soon! 👋
